the creation of humanitarian spaces and the humanitarianization of spaces of im/mobilities.
the humanitarian responses to the bordering of the sea, land and people, and the making of the humanitarian borderscape in the context of the current migration crisis.
the ways in which humanitarianism is being transformed and reconfigured in response to the current migration crisis, and the role of MSF in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

humanitarian borderscapes are not only spaces of care, but also spaces of power, where humanitarian actors and their activities are not only shaped by the dynamics of mobility, but also contribute to the production of these dynamics.

the humanitarian response to irregular mobility in Europe is shaped by the border and that the humanitarian borderscape has specific characteristics, which can be identified through a focus on the multiplicity of actors and the multiplicity of spaces in which they operate.
the humanitarian borderscape is a space where the border is not a fixed line or place but a space where the humanitarian is a border-making practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been trying to understand what happens when humanitarian actors and humanitarian spaces are placed in a border context.
the humanitarian border is an assemblage of multiple actors, spaces, practices and technologies that produce specific types of mobility.
it is a humanitarian borderscape, which is a result of the im/ mobilities of people and the specificities of the border and which is shaped by multiple actors and practices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
humanitarian responses to migration and displacement are not only about saving lives, but also about the production of particular humanitarian borderscapes.
the humanitarian response to irregular migration in Europe is not a coherent, linear process, but a fragmented, complex and dynamic one.
